body:
A vape that refuses to charge is frustrating, especially when you rely on it daily, but several of the causes are easy to find and fix. The problem is usually the cable, the power source, dirt in the charging port or a battery that has been left completely flat. Sometimes it is a genuine fault, and in a few cases it is a sign that the device should not be used. This guide walks through the checks in the best order, explains what each light pattern might mean, covers disposables with and without charging ports, lists what to avoid, explains when to stop and what to do with a device that is damaged or hot, and tells you how to get help. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive.

## First: is it meant to be rechargeable?
Many disposables have no charging port and cannot be charged. Check the product page and the device. A rechargeable device has a visible port, usually USB-C, at the bottom or the side. If there is no port, the device is non-rechargeable, and when the battery is flat, it is finished. See [rechargeable versus non-rechargeable disposables](/blog/rechargeable-vs-non-rechargeable-disposables/).

## 1. Try another cable
Cables fail more often than devices. Test a different USB-C or micro-USB cable known to work, for example one that charges your phone. Check the cable for fraying, kinks or a loose connector. Some cables are for power only or have poor wiring, and some very thin cables do not carry enough current. Use a good-quality cable.

## 2. Try another power source
Use a standard 5V adapter or a different USB port. Some chargers that deliver high-power fast charging may not work with small devices, and some computer ports supply too little power. A plain 5-volt adapter of the type used for phones is usually best. If you are using a power bank, try a wall adapter instead.

## 3. Check the charging port
Lint and dirt can block contact. With the device off, gently clear the port with a wooden toothpick or compressed air. Do not use metal tools, because they can short the contacts or bend the pins. Look into the port with a torch. If you see a bent pin, corrosion or liquid, do not try to charge it. Liquid in the port is a common problem in devices that have leaked, so see [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).

## 4. Look at the lights
No light on charge may mean a dead battery or fault. A light that blinks in a pattern may be a code, for example for low battery, charging or a fault. See [understanding vape device indicator lights](/blog/understanding-vape-device-indicator-lights/). Check the manual for what each pattern means. Some devices show no light for the first few minutes of charging a very flat battery.

## 5. Leave it for a while
Deeply discharged batteries may need a few minutes before showing any charging response, because the protection circuit lets only a small current through at first. Leave the device connected for 10 to 15 minutes, and check for a light or warmth. Do not leave it unattended while it charges, and unplug it if it gets hot.

## 6. Avoid heat and damage
Do not charge a device that is hot, swollen or damaged. If the device feels hot, unplug it and let it cool away from flammable items. A swollen casing means the battery is failing. Stop using it, and follow the [disposal guidance](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). A device that has been dropped may have internal damage even if it looks fine.

## 7. Check the temperature
Charging a very cold battery can harm it, and many devices refuse to charge outside a temperature range. If the device has been in the cold, let it warm to room temperature before you charge it. If it has been in the heat, let it cool.

## 8. Not rechargeable?
Disposables without a charging port cannot be charged. If the battery is flat, the device has reached the end of its life. Replace it, and dispose of the old one properly.

## What the symptoms might mean
- **No light, no response:** a dead battery, a faulty cable or a faulty port.
- **Light flashes briefly then stops:** a protection circuit, a poor connection or a fault.
- **It charges but the battery drains quickly:** an old or damaged battery.
- **It charges very slowly:** a weak adapter or a damaged cable.
- **It gets hot while charging:** stop immediately and unplug it.

## A step-by-step routine
1. Confirm the device is rechargeable.
2. Try a different cable.
3. Try a different adapter or port.
4. Check and gently clean the port.
5. Leave it connected for 10 to 15 minutes.
6. Look for light patterns and compare with the manual.
7. If there is no change, stop and consider the device faulty.

## Safety and care
Follow [battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/). Charge on a hard, flat surface, not on a bed or sofa. Do not leave a device charging unattended or overnight. Use a reputable charger. If something smells odd, smokes or gets very hot, stop, move away from flammable items and call emergency services if there is a fire risk.

## When it is faulty
If a device we supplied will not charge, contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order ID, what you tried and a photo of the device and the port. Check the [refund policy](/refunds/) for what applies. Do not try to open or repair it. Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) if you need a replacement.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does my device charge but not turn on?
The battery may be very flat. Leave it connected a while. If it still does not work, the battery or the electronics may be faulty.

### Can I use a phone charger?
Usually yes, if it is a standard 5-volt USB adapter and the device uses a standard cable. Avoid unbranded chargers.

### Why is the light green already?
Some devices show green when a short charge is enough, or when the battery is full. If the device still does not work, the battery may be worn.

### Can I charge a device that got wet?
No. Let it dry completely, away from heat, and do not charge it until the port is dry. If it still does not work, it may be faulty.

### Is it normal for a device to get warm?
Slightly warm is normal. Hot to touch is not. Unplug it.

Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Case studies
### The cable that looked fine
A customer's device would not charge for days. A different cable fixed it at once. The first cable had a broken wire inside, which could not be seen. Lesson: always try another cable first.

### The lint in the port
A device that lived in a pocket stopped charging. A wooden toothpick removed a plug of lint from the port, and it charged normally. Lesson: pockets collect lint, and ports are small.

### The over-discharged battery
A device that had been left in a drawer for months showed no response. After 15 minutes connected, a light finally pulsed, and it charged. Lesson: very flat batteries need patience, and are not always dead.

### The swollen device
A device that had been left in a hot car for weeks had a swollen case and would not charge. It was retired and disposed of at a recycling site. Lesson: a swollen device is finished, whatever the light says.

## A short list of charging do's and don'ts
- Do use a good cable and a standard 5V adapter.
- Do charge on a hard, flat surface.
- Do stay nearby and unplug when full.
- Do not charge a hot, wet, swollen or damaged device.
- Do not use metal tools in the port.
- Do not leave it charging overnight.

## When to replace instead of repair
If the device is a disposable, replace it. If it is a pod or tank system and the port is damaged, replacing the battery unit may be the only option, because ports are hard to repair. Do not attempt soldering or opening the device. The cost of a replacement is small next to the cost of an incident.

## Frequently asked questions about charging problems
### Why does my device charge on one cable and not another?
Cables differ in quality and in the current they carry. A cable that works for one device may not suit another. Use a good one.

### Does a vape need a special charger?
Usually a standard 5V USB adapter and the right cable are enough. Check the manual for any special requirements.

### Should I take the device to a repair shop?
Sealed devices are not repairable, and opening them is risky. For devices from us, contact us first.

### Can a drop cause charging problems?
Yes. A drop can loosen internal connections or damage the port. If problems began after a drop, stop using it if it is damaged.

### One more thing to check
If you have tried everything and the device still will not charge, check that you are plugging into the right port. Some devices have more than one opening, such as a charging port and an airflow hole, and it is easy to mistake one for the other. Look at the product page or manual for the position of the port. If you are certain it is the right one and nothing works, contact us for help.
